title: Recovery Phrase Safety Basics
plain:
Your recovery phrase (sometimes called seed words) is the master key to your bitcoin. Whoever holds it can spend your funds. If you lose it and your device fails, your bitcoin is gone forever.

Write the phrase by hand on paper, or stamp it into metal. Keep it offline at all times. Paper can burn or flood; metal survives fire and water.

Never type your seed words into a website, app, chat message, email, spreadsheet, or any "verification" form. Legitimate software and support staff will never ask for them. Anyone who does is attempting theft.

Never photograph your phrase or store it in a cloud account, password manager, or notes app. Anything connected to the internet can be breached.

Keep at least two copies in different secure locations, so one disaster cannot destroy every backup. Consider tamper-evident storage so you can tell whether a copy has been accessed.

If a website, caller, or "wallet support" agent asks you to read your phrase aloud or enter it to "unlock", "verify", or "migrate" funds, stop. It is always a scam.

Practise recovery safely: confirm you can restore your wallet using a small amount before you rely on it for savings.
technical: A BIP-39 recovery phrase encodes the entropy of a hierarchical deterministic wallet (BIP-32). Possession of the phrase permits full private-key derivation, so exposure equals total key compromise and loss equals irrecoverable funds. Best practice is offline generation on a dedicated hardware device, physical backup media, and an optional BIP-39 passphrase stored separately, recognizing that a passphrase introduces its own loss risk. Any online entry of the phrase, even once, should be treated as a compromise requiring migration to fresh entropy.
